correctness.rationale: For complete multipartite graphs with at least three parts, the TOIDS condition is equivalent to the complement lying within one part. The three-block construction follows immediately. The four-block obstruction is exhaustive: after fixing one coalition pair, every other block lies in one part; any partner choice for one such block either makes an original block a TOIDS or makes a purported coalition union lie within one part and fail total domination. Exhaustive finite checks independently confirm the characterization and exact value for every noncomplete profile of order at most eight.

value.rationale: The result fills the canonical complete-multipartite family immediately adjacent to the initiating paper’s clique and biclique computations. It reveals a sharp structural phase change: the bipartite value can grow with a shore size, while every noncomplete graph with at least three parts has the constant value three. The proof identifies the mechanism—TOIDS complements are trapped in one part—and gives a complete exact classification for this natural regime rather than a routine numerical instance.
